newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares end easier in drifting market.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares end easier in drifting market.

text.p: * NZ shares close easier in drifting market
* Brash comments not seen affecting market adversely
* Air NZ shares gain ahead of rights closure on Tuesday
New Zealand shares ended slightly easier on Monday in a market currently devoid of any real focus, brokers said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 4.84 points weaker at 2,330.05, with all leading stocks either flat or softer on the day.

However, brokers said Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's call for fiscal restraint to curtail the New Zealand dollar had had little impact on the market and an easing in monetary policy was still expected in December.
Interest in Telecom's half year profit result on Thursday had been heightened by the company's acknowledgement it was looking at the possibility of a share buy-back.

The market leader closed two cents weaker at NZ$7.58, hampered by a sell-off in the bond market, but brokers expect it to remain at around current levels until Thursday, when any announcement is most likely to be made.
Air New Zealand rights rose as investors bought in ahead of the expiry of the issue on Tuesday. The 'B' rights rose 14 to $1.35 and the 'A' rights were up ten, also to $1.35.
Air NZ shares also gained, the 'B' shares rising ten cents to $3.40 and the 'A' shares up six to $2.54.

Brokers said trade was heavy in Fletcher Energy, which ended five cents stronger at $4.06. "People obviously still like the story there," said Tim Koller at Hendry Hay McIntosh, who noted that one crossing in the stock of two million shares at $4.05 was the largest trade of the day.
Independent Newspapers Plc exchangeable shares listed today at NZ$8.30 but ended at $8.20 on very small on-market trade, while INL shares dipped 15 cents to $7.05.
